children: Macrogenics shares fell Monday after trial data for its investigational cancer treatment lorigerlimab showed high rates of severe side effects, including one patient death, as well as a high dropout rate.

The biopharmaceutical company said the bispecific antibody yielded a 25% confirmed objective response rate in advanced clear cell gynecologic cancer patients during the Phase 2 Linnet study, according to interim results.

However, MacroGenics reported that 49% of treated patients experienced Grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events, or TRAEs, including one patient death from treatment-related complications in the trial's platinum-resistant ovarian cancer cohort.
The most common TRAEs were anemia, decreased count in neutrophil--a common white blood cell--and an increase in the enzyme aspartate aminotransferase, the company said.
Nearly a quarter of the trial patients discontinued the therapy, it said.
As a result, MacroGenics said it will test lower doses on a new cohort and plans to report the updated study results in the first half of 2027.
The company noted that the proposed drug demonstrated a 44% disease-control rate, and that all responding patients remained in response at the time of the data cutoff, which was Sept. 1.

title: MacroGenics Stock Tumbles as Patient Death, Severe Side Effects Cloud Cancer-Drug Data
